$comment: What one golden run of the LLM tool registry COSTS on the input side, per operation, in characters. Read on every CI run by scripts/llm-budget.mjs (`npm run llm:budget:check`, inside check:ci) and re-recorded by `npm run llm:budget -- --accept --reason "..."`. The gate the quality bake cannot be: quality says the output is still good, this says the request did not quietly get more expensive. Characters rather than tokens because a character count is exact on every machine; the token and USD figures the report prints are estimates.
acceptedReason: seeded from a static upper bound on each registry entry (the byte span of its system:/prompt: block plus its golden's serialized schema), measured without executing the registry — so every ceiling here is ABOVE what the script measures, by roughly 20-50%. The first `--accept` run replaces them with measured values + MARGIN and the gate tightens.
$pricing: Mirrors the GEMINI_MODEL input rate in src/lib/llm/cost.ts (flash tier, the model production serves with). Used only to print a dollar figure next to the character count — nothing is enforced on it, and it is not billing.
$run: The uniform-drift ceiling: every operation can stay under its own line while the whole run grows. Sum of the seeded upper bounds, rounded up.

history.reason: seeded from static upper bounds, not from a run — totalInputChars is null because nothing measured it. The next --accept fills it in.
